area: Traffic analysis: ZIA app services and app service groups (the Office 365 One Click rule's OFFICE365) matched with Microsoft's published Microsoft 365 endpoint list in the Path analyzer, its what-if, DNS Control, workload forwarding, Test a list and Shadowed rules (app_services.py, m365_endpoints.py), and the optional, off-by-default fetch of that list (Advanced settings)
title: Microsoft 365 app service groups matched by host name and address, with the list treated as untrusted and every gap left unknown

checks.what: Membership source in the tenant: zscaler-sdk-python 1.11.3 models an app service and an app service group as id, name and isNameL10nTag only (zia/models/cloud_firewall_app_services.py) and has no endpoint that lists their members; Client Connector's IP-based apps (zcc/predefined_ip_based_apps.py, zcc/web_app_service.py) are a different object with no documented link to a ZIA app service, so they are not used

Oracle of 30 destinations against the OFFICE365 group: exact hosts, case and trailing dot, '*.domain' (one or more labels, never the apex or a look-alike), '*' inside a label and Microsoft's tenant placeholder (one label part), an IDN in punycode, IPv4, IPv6, bracketed and IPv4-mapped addresses, ports Microsoft publishes or not

Unknown stays the fallback: no list, a stale list (30 days, settable 1-365), a host name not in the list (its address is not resolved), a port outside the set's ports, an app service that is not Microsoft 365, a damaged kept file

The list as untrusted input: 23 malformed shapes refused whole with a reason (not a list, not JSON, NaN, deep nesting, a missing or repeated id, a bad host pattern or placeholder, an address, a port), a 2 MB cap before parsing, at most 2000 sets and 50,000 entries, and a refused list never replaces the one kept

The fetch: off by default (no request leaves the machine, Fetch now is a 409), then GET only to https://endpoints.office.com (other schemes, hosts, ports and credentials refused before a request), no redirect followed, a 10-second timeout, TLS verified, a random clientrequestid and nothing about the tenant, the version first and the list only when it changed, a failure recorded and not retried within the hour

Path analyzer, what-if, DNS Control and Cloud & Branch Connector forwarding rules: the One Click rule decides a Microsoft 365 host definitely, an address outside the ranges falls to the next rule definitely, and without the list it is never a match
Test a list: rows that share a trace never mix a Microsoft 365 address with another; QUIC and Teams media to Microsoft 365 are allowed by the One Click rule and the same ports elsewhere blocked

Shadowed rules: a later firewall rule is reported hidden by the One Click rule only when every host name, CIDR and range it names is a published Microsoft 365 endpoint on every port its network services allow, by a current list; 12 near misses (an outside address, an unlisted host, a wider block, a range past the block, no or another port, unread services, an IP group, another group, a stale list) report nothing

Advanced settings: the section starts off, every control is labelled, keyboard reachable and has help, the status is set from escaped text, and switching, importing and removing are audited; the destination is listed with the other outbound calls in SECURITY.md

findings.title: The Office 365 One Click rule's app service group (OFFICE365) was always 'unknown': the Path analyzer, its what-if, DNS Control, workload forwarding and Test a list reported Microsoft 365 traffic the rule allows as conditional, and Shadowed rules could not compare it
findings.fix: app_services.criterion matches it by host name and address against Microsoft's published Microsoft 365 endpoint list (m365_endpoints), with unknown kept for everything the list cannot settle; shadow_rules compares it with a later rule's destinations and ports

findings.title: Found while building, never released: Test a list shared one trace between destinations its host index saw alike, so an address outside Microsoft 365 took a Microsoft 365 address's One Click allow
findings.fix: bulk_test.PathEvaluator's fingerprint includes the Microsoft 365 endpoint sets that hold the destination whenever a firewall or DNS rule names an app service

findings.title: Test a list counted a rule unknown only on its app service group as 'blocks in some contexts' (a user, a time), although it is the destination that is not known
findings.fix: bulk_test._context_only leaves app service criteria out of the context labels

notes: Assumed (not in the SDK or the API reference): Zscaler's OFFICE365 group holds Microsoft's published endpoints.
Assumed: the app service names that mean Microsoft 365 (app_services.M365_NAMES).
Assumed: the app services and groups a rule names are alternatives (any one is enough).
A host name not in the list is unknown, because its address is not resolved.
Microsoft's wildcard and Microsoft's tenant placeholder semantics are read strictly: fewer matches, never more.
